page: Amazon Web Services r5.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by custom Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL processors delivering 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at a 3.1 GHz clock frequency. The architecture utilizes an x86_64 instruction set with hardware extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA. For memory capacity, the host provides 768.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio across its dedicated allocation. Network throughput is backed by a 25 Gbps baseline interconnect, while local instance storage is absent, necessitating network-attached storage via EBS.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel throughput and high memory capacity utilization. In stress-ng testing, multi-core CPU performance scored in the top tier at 80,919.72, despite single-core performance landing in the bottom quartile at 1,383.99. Memory bandwidth tests confirmed strong metrics, recording 220.3 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 98.33 GB/sec on large-block writes. PassMark suites echo these findings with top-tier ratings across overall CPU compute (55,744.75), memory operations (2,764.89), and database operations (21,687.95). In application benchmarks, the server reached 74.62 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 46.46 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the r5.24xlarge is its deliberate focus on aggregate core count and memory volume over single-threaded speed and specialized acceleration. While parallel throughput is extensive, single-threaded operations such as gzip compression sit in the lower percentiles. The absence of discrete GPUs also limits token generation capabilities, registering poor throughput on medium LLM models (6.02 tokens/sec on 7B). As a large-footprint memory-optimized node, it yields favorable resource density for multi-threaded in-memory databases, distributed caching, and large analytical datasets that demand substantial DDR4 capacity without GPU acceleration.
description: Amazon Web Services r5.24xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by 96 vCPUs (48 physical cores) using Intel Xeon 8259CL processors operating at 3.1 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro System using the x86_64 architecture, it contains 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory at an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, paired with 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance features no local storage or GPUs, relying on external network-attached storage. Benchmark testing highlights top-quartile multi-core CPU output, database performance, and memory bandwidth, reaching 74.62 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 220.3 GB/sec in large-block memory reads. However, single-core execution and sequential text generation on language models remain comparatively weak. The system is suited for large in-memory databases, caching layers, big data analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise application workloads.
